premise: After my father’s sudden death, his will left my twin brother and me his $245,000 collection of vintage neon signs, but he forged a bill of sale and sold the entire collection to a roadside museum for $90,000, claiming I’d agreed to split the cash; years later I found the museum’s display with a plaque crediting my father’s name, exposed the forgery, sued my brother for conversion and won the museum’s acquisition contract void — I now run a ‘Broken Trust’ beer garden where every neon sign in the collection hangs behind the bar, and my brother is obligated to polish them every weekend under a court order.
